label: fed-back digit 1 during copy phase
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, only when the input token is the digit 1 (the model feeding back its own earlier output of 1). Never fires in the original phase or on the delimiter, and never on any other input token. Strongest when the 1 is fed back early in the copy (recall_idx 2, i.e. original token 1 was 1, e.g. h 1 1 ... -> activation ~1.0 of max). Activation shrinks for later positions and for the second or third consecutive 1 (often weak or silent). The 1 fed back at recall_idx 1 (sequence starting with 1) gives only weak activation. Many late-position fed-back 1s near the end of the sequence are inactive, which accounts for most false positives.

issues: Most claims hold. The feature is active 0 times in the original phase and on the delimiter. Every activation has in_tok == 1. 'Copy phase & in_tok==1' gives recall 1.0 and precision 0.699 on dev. Adding recall_idx >= 2 gives test P 0.826, R 0.961, F1 0.888, mass recall 0.986, matching the reported scores.

Magnitude claims hold. recall_idx==2 has the most activation mass (0.38) and the top examples are 'x 1 1 ...' with the second 1 at roughly 0.3-0.5 of max. A 1 at recall_idx 1 (sequence starting with 1) fires weakly: precision 0.146, activations around 0.05-0.07 of max.

Minor inaccuracy about where the false positives fall. Precision on fed-back 1s does drop with recall_idx (0.98 at idx 2, 0.96 at 3, 0.84 at 4, 0.70 at 5, 0.61 at 6+). But it does not drop near the end of the sequence. to_go==0 has the highest precision of any to_go value (0.74), against 0.67 at to_go==5. So the silent 1s are late in the copy, far from <DEL>, not specifically at the end.

The false positives are graded falloff, not a crisp class. Splitting by L, prev_tok type, in_count or n_digits gives no clean subset; precision stays around 0.55-0.8 among late 1s. Excluding late or repeated 1s lowers test F1: recall_idx 2..5 gives 0.844, and excluding prev_tok==1 gives 0.879.
